instantiated_cells.justification: The definition of "legislative agent" turns on being "engaged ... to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes" with no monetary compensation threshold; registration is required within ten days of engagement regardless of compensation amount.
Registration is triggered by engagement of a legislative agent within ten days, not by any expenditure dollar threshold — the statute imposes no minimum expenditure amount for registration.

Itemization of meals/food/beverage expenditures per public officer is required only when cumulative payments by the legislative agent during a calendar year exceed $50 to/for that particular official.

Each legislative agent and employer must file expenditure statements with each updated registration statement (January, May, September) showing total expenditures, with no minimum-dollar threshold below which filing is excused.
The statute requires filing expenditure statements with each updated registration regardless of time spent lobbying; no percentage-of-time de minimis exemption from filing exists.

content.text:
I'll analyze the Ohio statute for each threshold question.

**Compensation threshold**: §101.70(F) defines "legislative agent" as one engaged to "actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes" — no dollar threshold for compensation.

**Expenditure threshold for registration**: Registration is triggered by engagement, not by expenditure amount. §101.72(A) requires filing within 10 days of engagement — no dollar threshold.

**Time percent threshold**: §101.70(F) says "engaged during at least a portion of the individual's time to actively advocate as one of the individual's main purposes" — qualitative "main purpose" standard, not a numeric percentage.

**Itemization de minimis**: §101.73(B)(3) sets a $50 cumulative annual threshold for itemizing meals/food/beverages per official.

**Filing de minimis dollars**: No dollar threshold to trigger filing itself — statements are required with each updated registration regardless of amount.

**Filing de minimis time percent**: No percentage time threshold in the statute.

Each legislative agent and employer must file expenditure statements with each updated registration statement (January, May, September) showing total expenditures, with no minimum-dollar threshold below which filing is excused.
